repo_model.summary: This repository is a RelBench candidate workspace: main.py loads a task from the sanitized cache and emits validation/test NumPy predictions, while kapso_evaluation/grader.py runs the candidate, scores official validation metrics, and archives full-fidelity runs.

entrypoints.how_to_run: python main.py --debug for the cheap-build mode, or python main.py for a full run.
python kapso_evaluation/grader.py --fidelity fast|full [--fraction F] [--seed S], with the required RelBench environment variables set.

where_to_edit.role: Primary candidate implementation: load data, train or fit models, and generate validation/test predictions.
Reusable task loading, output saving, debug detection, temporal-safety, and recommendation-metric helpers.
Read-only local validator for prediction files before submitting to the grader.

claims.statement: The executable candidate reads RELBENCH_DATASET and RELBENCH_TASK, loads the RelBench task with download=False, and determines validation and test row counts from task tables.

evidence.description: Reads the dataset identity from the environment.
Reads the task identity from the environment.
Loads the task without downloading.
Determines the test row count from the task table.

claims.statement: The seeded baseline branches by task family: recommendations repeat destination IDs 0 through K-1, binary classification predicts 0.5, multiclass classification predicts a uniform distribution, and other tasks predict the training-target median.

evidence.description: Begins the recommendation-task branch.
Creates the baseline recommendation row of IDs.
Creates constant binary predictions.
Creates uniform multiclass predictions.
Computes the regression-style training median.

claims.statement: Predictions are written as val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy under KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; non-rolling runs write both files, while rolling invocations always write test predictions and omit validation output for the empty validation snapshot.

evidence.description: Gets the evaluator-provided output directory.
Writes validation predictions only outside rolling mode.
Always writes test predictions.

claims.statement: The provided grader runs main.py in an isolated child subprocess with fidelity-specific timeouts, then loads the generated artifacts and computes official RelBench validation metrics.

evidence.description: Documents isolated execution of the candidate.
Builds the candidate command for fast or full fidelity.
Starts the candidate as a subprocess.
Computes the task's official validation metrics.

claims.statement: kapso_datasets.common provides the standard data-flow helpers: it loads the dataset, task, database, and train/validation/test tables, and saves both prediction arrays in the evaluator output directory.

evidence.description: Defines the sanitized-cache task loader.
Builds the RelBench database without downloading.
Loads the training table.
Loads the test table.
Defines the shared prediction-saving helper.

claims.statement: The general contract requires val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy after every run, with rows positionally aligned to the task validation and test tables.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every run.
Requires positional row alignment to the task tables.
Checks that both prediction artifacts exist.

claims.statement: Prediction formats are task-specific: binary outputs are float probabilities in [0,1] with shape (N,), regression outputs are float (N,), multiclass outputs are float (N,C), and recommendation outputs are integer ranked destination IDs with shape (N,K).

evidence.description: Defines binary and regression prediction formats.
Defines multiclass and recommendation formats.
Checks non-recommendation shapes.
Checks binary probability bounds.

claims.statement: Validation predictions must be out-of-sample: the model producing validation predictions must not have trained on validation labels; using train plus validation is allowed only for the model producing test predictions.

evidence.description: Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample.
Specifies the permitted train-plus-validation pattern for test prediction models.

claims.statement: The search score is the official validation metric named by RELBENCH_PRIMARY_METRIC; test labels and test metrics are unavailable inside the sanitized evaluation loop.

evidence.description: Reads the configured primary metric.
Evaluates predictions on the validation table.
Places the primary validation metric in the manifest score.
States that test predictions cannot be scored in the loop.

claims.statement: Data must be loaded from the sanitized cache using the RelBench APIs with download=False; test labels are physically absent and must not be probed for.

evidence.description: Requires download=False access to the sanitized cache.
States that test labels are absent.
Loads the dataset with download=False.
Loads the task with download=False.

claims.statement: After writing predictions, run python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py to verify both files, shapes, finite values, recommendation dtypes/ranges, and binary probability bounds.

evidence.description: Recommends running the prediction checker before grading.
Checks both validation and test splits.
Checks prediction shapes.
Checks finite numeric values.

claims.statement: A fast official dry run uses the grader's fast fidelity, which invokes main.py --debug while still scoring the complete validation split.

evidence.description: Defines fast fidelity as the candidate's cheap-build mode.
States that fast runs main.py --debug.
States that both fidelities score the complete validation split.
Recommends verifying the environment with a fast dry run.

claims.statement: A successful official evaluation prints the validation metrics and a KAPSO_EVAL_MANIFEST line whose score is the configured primary validation metric.

evidence.description: Prints official validation metrics.
Sets the manifest score from the primary metric.
Emits the machine-readable manifest marker.

claims.statement: Rolling evaluation is a special per-tick protocol: an empty val.parquet makes main.py enter rolling mode and omit val_predictions.npy, while the rolling grader consumes each tick's test_predictions.npy and assembles the final validation/test vectors.

evidence.description: Documents the empty validation table in rolling snapshots.
Uses val.parquet existence to determine the validation count.
Sets rolling mode when the validation count is zero.
Reads each tick's test_predictions.npy.
Saves the assembled vector for the current split.

claims.statement: Fast fidelity does not reduce the scored item set: it only adds --debug to the candidate command, and fraction/seed are recorded in the manifest rather than used to subsample validation rows.

evidence.description: Explains that evaluation cost is in the candidate build.
Defines fast mode as main.py --debug.
States that fraction and seed are echoed for validation.
States that the scored item set never shrinks.

claims.statement: In normal load_and_score processing, the grader explicitly validates validation predictions but only checks that test_predictions.npy exists and can be loaded; use check_predictions.py to catch test-side shape or value errors.

evidence.description: Defines the validation and test artifact paths.
Loads validation predictions.
Loads test predictions without subsequent normal-mode shape validation.
Begins the explicit validation contract checks.
The local checker validates both splits.

claims.statement: The candidate and evaluation suite require NumPy and the RelBench Python package.

evidence.description: Imports NumPy.
Imports RelBench task classes.
States that Python with relbench and numpy is sufficient for the suite.

claims.statement: Runtime configuration is supplied through environment variables, including dataset/task identity, primary metric, cache and work directories, timeouts, and the candidate output directory.

evidence.description: Introduces the exported environment configuration.
Lists the primary metric and work directory variables.
Lists cache and shared-cache variables.
Sets KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR for the child candidate.

book.summary: This repository is a RelBench candidate workspace: main.py loads a task from the sanitized cache and emits validation/test NumPy predictions, while kapso_evaluation/grader.py runs the candidate, scores official validation metrics, and archives full-fidelity runs.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: Candidate generation, contract validation, and official scoring are separated into the root program, starter helpers, and provided grader.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the candidate directly for debug/full modes or invoke the provided grader for official evaluation.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Implement the candidate in main.py and reuse the contract-aware helpers in kapso_datasets.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction artifacts, data access, validation methodology, and scoring must follow the RelBench contract.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use the local contract checker and a fast official grader run to validate changes.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: Rolling snapshots, fidelity semantics, and asymmetric grader checks can invalidate otherwise plausible candidate changes.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The runtime depends on Python, NumPy, RelBench, and handler-provided environment configuration.
